key_insight: An adaptive measurement-feedback controller can learn quantum state preparation using only experimentally observed measurement history, without access to full quantum-state information.
engineering_relevance: The approach is hardware-compatible and scalable because it replaces state reconstruction with online policy learning and one-shot measurement-based rewards.
method: Use reinforcement learning under partial observability to select measurement operators and feedback actions in real time.
Build the reward from stochastic terminal measurements of randomly sampled Hamiltonian terms to estimate target energy unbiasedly.
Train and validate on ground-state preparation and entangled-state generation tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on ground states of the Bose--Hubbard model and GHZ-state generation, indicating performance on both many-body and entanglement-preparation benchmarks.
watch_item: Training and reward estimation may be sensitive to measurement noise and sampling variance, especially as system size grows.
paper_title: Experiment-compatible measurement--feedback quantum state preparation with reinforcement learning
